The words

At early dawn, with pious thought,
The holy women spices brought —
For Christ, their Lord, was dead; —
But lo! the stone was rolled away:
"Where are the seals?" they wondering say,
"The guard, where He was laid?"

"Why with your ointments mix your tears?
Why all this sighing, and those fears?"
An angel near declares:
"There lies the stone that barred the tomb,
No longer now its solemn gloom
Your Lord and Master shares."

"Haste, haste with joy the tidings tell,
The Lord hath vanquished death and hell,
For He, the Death of death,
Hath burst asunder hades prison,
And, first-born from the dead hath risen,
Even as afore He saith."

Honour to Thee, O Christ, we bring,
Thy glorious rising now we sing,
Victorious is Thy strife;
Our Hope, our Trust, on Thee we call,
Our Joy, our Strength, our God, our All,
And our Immortal Life.

How to sing it from the solfa

  • Find doh first. Play or hum Eb and sing d r m f s up from it, so the whole choir has the key in their ears before you start.
  • Pitch the first note. The tune starts on d (E♭), on the word “At”, as a pickup before the first full bar.
  • Count the time. 3/2 means three minim beats in each bar. In the grid every cell is half a crotchet: a dash (–) holds the note before it, and _ is a rest.
  • Know the notes. The tune uses d r m f s l t and the chromatic fe. A comma after a note (s,) is the octave below; an apostrophe (d') is the octave above.

About the hymn

John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the Greek Office Books (Paisley, 1904), headed “Centos And Suggestions”.

The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Particular Metre (8.8.6.8.8.6), and this page sets them to MERIBAH; any other Common Particular Metre tune fits them as well.

  • Words: Traditional Greek
  • Translated (1904): John Brownlie (1857–1925)
  • Music (1839): Lowell Mason (1792–1872)

Questions about At Early Dawn, with Pious Thought

What is the doh of At Early Dawn, with Pious Thought?

In this version, in Eb major, doh is Eb. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does At Early Dawn, with Pious Thought start on?

It starts on d (E♭ in Eb major), a pickup on the word “At” before the first full bar. Find doh first, then sing up or down to d.

Is At Early Dawn, with Pious Thought in the public domain?

Yes. John Brownlie died in 1925, Lowell Mason died in 1872; the words were in print by 1904 and the music in 1839. Everyone named died before 1955 and both were published before 1929, so the hymn is out of copyright in the UK, the EU, the United States and Nigeria. Modern arrangements and translations can still be under copyright.
